timeline.label: resolved
timeline.body: On November 16, 2026, between 09:30 and 15:55 UTC, some pull request merges on GitHub timed out. On average, 2.9% of merge attempts timed out, with a peak of 7.1% at 15:17 UTC. Some GitHub Actions workflow runs triggered by pull requests were also delayed. Git operations such as push and fetch stayed available, with higher latency. This was a repeat of a shorter event on November 13, between 13:15 and 17:50 UTC, when 1.7% of merges timed out. Both events had the same cause: some of the storage servers that hold Git repository data reached their disk read bandwidth limits. A merge must be written to every copy of a repository, so one overloaded server slowed merges for every repository it hos

incidents.title: Disruption with some GitHub services
incidents.summary: Between November 5, 2026, at 18:02 UTC and November 19, 2026, at 18:05 UTC, GitHub users experienced unexpected expiration of their web browser sessions despite continued activity, requiring them to login. An authentication change introduced an issue that caused web requests to bypass the session activity updates and cookie renewal that normally extend session lifetime. Affected sessions consequently expired when they reached their initial expiration time. We mitigated the incident by deploying

timeline.label: resolved
timeline.body: Between November 5, 2026, at 18:02 UTC and November 19, 2026, at 18:05 UTC, GitHub users experienced unexpected expiration of their web browser sessions despite continued activity, requiring them to login. An authentication change introduced an issue that caused web requests to bypass the session activity updates and cookie renewal that normally extend session lifetime. Affected sessions consequently expired when they reached their initial expiration time. We mitigated the incident by deploying a fix to ensure that continued web activity renews session expiration and browser cookies. We are adding monitoring to detect unexpected drops in session renewal activity, helping us catch similar iss

timeline.label: monitoring
timeline.body: The degradation has been mitigated. We are monitoring to ensure stability.

timeline.label: monitoring
timeline.body: Starting around 18:02 UTC on November 5, GitHub web sessions stopped being renewed based on recent activity, so users were signed out when their sessions expired due to inactivity. These sign-outs were caused by a bug in session renewal, not due to a security incident. We believe we fixed the bug at 05:23 UTC on November 19, and sessions created since then should renew as usual. We’re continuing to monitor the situation. If you had an inactive session from that period, you may still find that you’re signed out when you return to GitHub. If that happens, all you need to do is sign back in.

timeline.label: investigating
timeline.body: We are investigating reports of impacted performance for some GitHub services.
